Senses.Explanation: The tiny mustard seed is the records’ scale-comparison object, repeatedly paired with reversals in which Mount Sumeru is contained within it. The graphs name a mustard seed. The allowlisted corpus has 507 hits in 163 files representing 160 independent works. Its small size supplies the comparison ‘mustard-seed-sized’ (芥子許, 76 hits in 54 files representing 54 independent works), as when a named record subject speaks of a doubt as small as a mustard seed. The corpus also repeatedly pairs the seed with Mount Sumeru in both directions: ‘Sumeru contains a mustard seed’ (須彌納芥子, 57 hits in 40 files representing 38 works) and ‘a mustard seed contains Sumeru’ (芥子納須彌, 71 hits in 56 files representing 54 works). In the Guizong encounter, Li Bo accepts the first statement but asks whether the second is false; Guizong asks where Li Bo’s ten thousand books are held in a body the size of a coconut. In another exchange, the two directions receive the one-word answers ‘easy’ and ‘difficult.’ A later address records mountains, earth, trees, monastics, laypeople, sages, and ordinary people placed inside a mustard seed without the seed becoming narrow. These are the corpus’s recorded scale constructions; the entry does not turn them into a symbolic meaning for the seed.
